Four functions, all taking and returning numpy float arrays (a scalar y0 is
accepted and treated as a 1-vector; `ys`/`xs`/`vs` are always 2-D,
shape (len(ts), dim)):

- `dp5_step(f, t, y, h) -> (y_new, err)`: one Dormand-Prince 5(4) step.
  `y_new` is the 5th-order solution, `err` is the difference between the 5th-
  and 4th-order solutions (the embedded error estimate).
- `rk5_fixed(f, t0, y0, t1, h) -> y(t1)`: `round((t1 - t0) / h)` steps of
  `dp5_step`.
- `dopri45(f, t0, y0, t1, rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-9) -> (ts, ys)`: adaptive step
  size control on the embedded estimate (RMS of err / (atol + rtol * max(|y|,
  |y_new|)) must be <= 1 to accept; grow and shrink the step with the usual
  safety factor and limits). `ts[0] == t0` and `ts[-1] == t1` exactly, every
  accepted step is recorded, and `t1 < t0` integrates backward.
- `verlet(accel, x0, v0, t0, t1, h) -> (xs, vs)`: velocity Stormer-Verlet
  (kick-drift-kick), `accel(x) -> a`, `round((t1 - t0) / h)` steps, initial
  state included.

The tests measure orders of convergence and long-time energy behaviour, not
just values, so the methods must actually be the methods named.

ts strictly monotone in the direction of integration.
    verlet-kdk-one-accel-per-step  verlet is velocity Verlet (half kick, drift, half kick). It reuses the last acceleration, so accel is called exactly n + 1 times and returns n + 1 rows.
    controller-as-specified  dopri45 accepts iff RMS(err / (atol + rtol*max(|y|, |y_new|))) <= 1. The factor is 0.9*norm^(-1/5), clamped to [0.2, 10] and capped at 1 right after a rejection. Steps are stretched to t1 when t + 1.01*h reaches t1.
    fixed-step-grid  rk5_fixed and verlet take n = max(1, round(|t1 - t0| / |h|)) steps of exactly (t1 - t0)/n. The final state is at t1, and the sign of h is ignored.
    shapes-and-dtypes  Scalar y0 is treated as a 1-vector. dp5_step and rk5_fixed return 1-D float arrays. ys, xs and vs are float arrays of shape (len(ts), dim). Caller inputs are never modified.
    backward-integration  All three drivers integrate backward when t1 < t0.
    fsal-call-count  dopri45 costs 2 f calls up front (f0 plus one probe) plus exactly 6 per attempted step.
    degenerate-span  t0 == t1 is a valid no-op: one row out and zero callback calls.
    no-infinite-loop  dopri45 raises RuntimeError when |h| falls below 10*eps*|t|, and a non-finite error norm is treated as a rejection rather than accepted.
    input-validation  Bad inputs fail loudly with ValueError: h == 0 or non-finite h in the fixed-step drivers, and y0, x0 or v0 with ndim > 1.
